$comment: Per-route first-load JS budgets, in KB gzipped. Enforced by
scripts/bundle-budget.mts, which runs in CI and fails the build.
── The spec's number, and why these are not it ──
PHASE-03-KUNDLI-UI.md §7 asks for < 180 KB gzipped on the kundli
route. Measured on 2026-09-18, that route is 198.6 KB and the floor
under it — React, react-dom and the Next client runtime, before a
single line of this product — is 159.5 KB. Two chunks account for
112 KB of that and contain no product code at all.
So 180 KB leaves about 20 KB for everything Ayana does, and the
i18n dictionaries alone are 14.8 KB. The target was set without
measuring the framework, and it is not reachable by trimming
product code. Recorded in PROJECT_STATUS.md as an unmet spec item
rather than quietly redefined.
── What these budgets ARE for ──
Catching regressions. Each is the measured size plus a small
allowance, so an import that drags in a date library or a second
copy of a corpus fails the build on the PR that adds it — which is
the thing a CI budget can actually deliver.
Lowering a number here is always allowed. Raising one is a decision
that should appear in a diff with a reason next to it.
